t:
(a) The second paragraph under the heading “Community Development Fund” in title III of division A of Public Law 109–115 is amended by striking “statement of managers accompanying this Act” and inserting “statement of managers correction for H.R. 3058 relating to the Economic Development Initiative submitted to the House of Representatives by the Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations of the House on November 18, 2005, and printed in the House section of the Congressional Record on such date”. 
    (b) Section 5023 of title V of division B of Public Law 109–148 is amended by striking “in title III of Public Law 109–115 (as in effect pursuant to H. Con. Res. 308, 109th Congress)” and inserting “in title III of division A of Public Law 109–115”. 
    (c) Each amendment made by this section shall apply as if included in the amended public law on the date of its enactment.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to a statement submitted by a committee chairman signals a consultative process. But the section only makes technical corrections to cross-references in earlier appropriations laws, and the only actors mentioned (the House and its Appropriations Committee chairman) are inside the federal government. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: submitted to the House of Representatives by the Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations of the House on November 18, 2005

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a previous law, correcting a reference to a legislative document (a statement of managers). It involves only internal congressional records and the Chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations. There is no consultation, coordination, or participation with any entity outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public). Congress and its committees are considered inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: amended by striking “statement of managers accompanying this Act” and inserting “statement of managers correction for H.R. 3058 relating to the Economic Development Initiative submitted to the House of Representatives by the Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations of the House on November 18, 2005, and printed in the House section of the Congressional Record on such date”

opus.w: This section only makes technical amendments that change cross-references in earlier public laws and sets their effective date. The submission to the House by a committee chairman may look procedural, but it happens entirely inside Congress, which is part of the federal government. No state, tribe, member of the public or other outside party is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period or right to sue.
opus.s: statement of managers correction for H.R. 3058 relating to the Economic Development Initiative submitted to the House of Representatives by the Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations of the House on November 18, 2005
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions a statement "submitted to the House of Representatives by the Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations." That sounds like a formal step in a decision process. But it is only a citation of a congressional document, and Congress is inside the federal government. The section is a set of technical amendments that fix cross-references, and no outside party takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutory text to correct a reference to a legislative document (a statement of managers). It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government. The entities involved (Congress, the Committee on Appropriations) are inside the federal government, and the action is purely textual correction.
qwen_chat.s: (a) The second paragraph under the heading “Community Development Fund” in title III of division A of Public Law 109–115 is amended by striking “statement of managers accompanying this Act” and inserting “statement of managers correction for H.R. 3058 relating to the Economic Development Initiative submitted to the House of Representatives by the Chairman of the Committee on Appropriations of the House on November 18, 2005, and printed in the House section of the Congressional Record on such date”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that referencing a "statement of managers" or the "Congressional Record" implies public access or participation. However, these are internal legislative documents and records. The section merely corrects textual references within the statute to point to the correct legislative history document. It does not create a process for outside parties to consult with the government, comment on a decision, or participate in an advisory capacity. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, and referencing their documents is not participation by outsiders.
